section: Agricultural marketing - APMC system, e-NAM, contract farming, model acts, FPOs, warehousing
subsections: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018
FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a feature of the Model APMC Act, 2003?
o: Whole State treated as one market area
Livestock and services brought within contract farming regulation
Contract farming kept outside the APMC framework
accepted.x: The Model APMC Act, 2003 permitted direct sale of agricultural produce to contract-farming sponsors. The other features are associated with the 2017 or 2018 model acts.
accepted.tq: Identify the feature belonging to the correct model act rather than a neighbouring reform.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The Model APLM Act, 2017 envisaged which one of the following arrangements?
o: Transfer of land title to the contract sponsor
Contract farming outside the APMC purview
The entire State as one market area
accepted.x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 proposed treating the whole State as one market area. Keeping contract farming outside the APMC purview and prohibiting transfer of land title are features of the 2018 Contract Farming Act.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive structural feature to distinguish the 2017 model act from the 2018 act.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with the Model APLM Act, 2017?
o: Contract farming — brought within the APMC purview
accepted.x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 included private yards, e-trading and livestock. Contract farming was kept outside the APMC purview by the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018.
accepted.tq: Find the feature wrongly transferred from one model act to another.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Model APMC Act, 2003 provided for special markets for perishables.
2. It provided for private markets.
3. It provided for common registration of intermediaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are features of the Model APMC Act, 2003: special markets for perishables, private markets and common registration of intermediaries.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the complete feature-list of the 2003 model act.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations correctly represents features of the Model APLM Act, 2017?
1. Warehouses as market yards
2. Single-point market fee
3. Unified licence
4. E-trading
accepted.x: The Model APLM Act, 2017 proposed warehouses as market yards, a single-point market fee, a unified licence and e-trading.
accepted.tq: Treat the listed institutional reforms as a connected package and eliminate partial combinations.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Karnataka's reformed agricultural market model is often cited as an example of
o: replacement of e-trading by barter exchange
accepted.x: Karnataka's reformed market model is frequently cited as a successful example of agricultural market reform.
accepted.tq: Recognise the State associated with the cited reform example.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Under the Model Agricultural Produce & Livestock Contract Farming and Services (Promotion & Facilitation) Act, 2018, which one of the following is correct?
o: The sponsor may purchase only a part of the pre-agreed quantity.
The sponsor automatically acquires title to the farmer's land.
The sponsor must purchase the entire pre-agreed quantity.
The sponsor may construct permanent structures on the farmer's land without restriction.
accepted.x: The sponsor is required to buy the entire pre-agreed quantity. The Act does not vest any right, title or interest in the farmer's land in the sponsor and prohibits permanent structures on it.
accepted.tq: Focus on the statutory obligation imposed on the sponsor and reject absolute ownership claims.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018:
1. Contract farming is kept outside the purview of the APMC Act.
2. The farmer is treated as the weaker party.
3. The Act covers livestock and services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2018 model act keeps contract farming outside the APMC Act, recognises the farmer as the weaker party and covers livestock and services.
accepted.tq: Verify the scope, protective approach and coverage of the 2018 model act.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018, which institution is responsible for online registration and recording of agreements?
accepted.x: Online registration is undertaken by the Registering and Agreement Recording Committee (RARC). Contract Farming Facilitation Groups operate at the village or panchayat level.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named institutions by matching each body with its specific function.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Contract Farming Facilitation Groups under the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018 are envisaged at which level?
accepted.x: Contract Farming Facilitation Groups (CFFGs) are envisaged at the village or panchayat level, enabling local facilitation and dispute settlement.
accepted.tq: Use the administrative level to distinguish CFFGs from the registration committee.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Model Contract Farming Act, 2018 is correct?
o: Disputes are automatically referred to civil courts in every case.
Disputes are to be settled only by a national tribunal.
Disputes are settled at the lowest level possible.
Disputes are excluded from the facilitation mechanism.
accepted.x: The model framework provides for settlement of disputes at the lowest level, thereby making the mechanism more accessible to farmers.
accepted.tq: Apply the decentralised dispute-resolution principle to the stated situation.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes contract farming?
o: Farmers exchange produce for inputs without any prior agreement.
Farmers sell produce to an agri-business firm at a price, quantity and/or time fixed in advance.
Farmers transfer ownership of their land to an agri-business firm for cultivation.
Farmers sell produce only through government procurement agencies at a price fixed after harvest.
accepted.x: Contract farming involves an agreement with an agri-business firm concerning the price, quantity and/or time of sale in advance. It does not involve transfer of land ownership.
accepted.tq: Separate a production-and-sale agreement from land transfer and post-harvest procurement.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The e-Choupal rural marketing network was started by
accepted.x: The e-Choupal rural marketing network was started by ITC.
accepted.tq: Match the branded rural marketing initiative with its implementing enterprise.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The Small Farmer Large Field model refers to a situation in which
o: large farmers divide their holdings into independent small plots
government agencies acquire private land for a single plantation
contract sponsors cultivate land after obtaining permanent title
marginal farmers organise into groups and harmonise their operations as one large field
accepted.x: Under the Small Farmer Large Field model, marginal farmers organise into groups and synchronise and harmonise operations so that the group functions like one large field.
accepted.tq: Translate the descriptive model into its operational meaning rather than its literal name.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The National Agriculture Market, e-NAM, was launched in
accepted.x: e-NAM was launched in 2016 as an electronic platform intended to integrate agricultural markets.
accepted.tq: Use the year as the decisive identifier among the reform milestones.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: As reported for e-NAM, which one of the following combinations is correct?
o: 1,522 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
1,522 mandis in 25 States and 2 Union Territories
1,225 mandis in 22 States and 5 Union Territories
1,050 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories
accepted.x: e-NAM covered 1,522 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories in the stated status report.
accepted.tq: Read the multi-part numerical figure as a single market-coverage combination.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The e-NAM platform was reported to have connected approximately how many farmers and traders?
accepted.x: The reported e-NAM figures were 1.79 crore farmers and 2.67 lakh traders.
accepted.tq: Distinguish crore and lakh magnitudes and avoid reversing the two stakeholder categories.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The grant mentioned for each mandi under e-NAM is
accepted.x: The grant provided under e-NAM is reported as ₹75 lakh per mandi.
accepted.tq: Separate the mandi-level grant from FPO-specific equity, credit and management support.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the reported agricultural trade through e-NAM in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The reported Andhra Pradesh figures were 33 markets, 9.88 lakh metric tonnes traded and a value of ₹5,054.86 crore.
accepted.tq: Keep the market count, physical quantity and monetary value in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Model Acts - APMC 2003, APLM 2017, Contract Farming 2018

accepted.s: The scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs was launched in
accepted.x: The Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs was launched in 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch year of the FPO scheme from the years of the model agricultural acts.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: The outlay approved for the Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs scheme is
accepted.x: The scheme has an outlay of ₹6,865 crore and provides support up to 2027-28.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its precise outlay rather than its target number.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Under the 10,000 FPO scheme, handholding support is provided for a period of
accepted.x: The scheme provides five years of handholding support through Cluster-Based Business Organisations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish handholding duration from the separate three-year management-support period.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s:
Which of the following organisations are named as implementing agencies of the 10,000 FPO scheme?
1. Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium
2. NABARD
3. NCDC
4. NAFED
accepted.x: SFAC, NABARD, NCDC and NAFED are named among the implementing agencies. NCDC also promotes cooperative-sector FPOs through the PACS route.
accepted.tq: Check the complete agency list instead of stopping after the first two familiar names.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which organisation is associated with promoting cooperative-sector FPOs, with a target of 1,100 through PACS?
accepted.x: NCDC promotes cooperative-sector FPOs, with a target of 1,100 FPOs through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS).
accepted.tq: Identify the agency from the distinctive cooperative-sector and PACS linkage.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a stated norm under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
o: At least 15% of FPOs are to be in Aspirational Districts.
Only one FPO may be formed in the entire State.
Every district must receive exactly 15 FPOs.
FPOs are prohibited from being linked with ONDC.
accepted.x: One stated norm is that 15% of FPOs should be located in Aspirational Districts. The scheme also envisages one FPO per block and linkage with ODOP and ONDC.
accepted.tq: Identify the valid percentage norm while rejecting absolute and prohibition-based distractors.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: The 10,000 FPO scheme envisages
o: one FPO per State, linked only to export markets
one FPO per district, with no product specialisation
one FPO per block, with ODOP and ONDC linkage
one FPO per village, without digital-market linkage
accepted.x: The scheme provides for one FPO per block and promotes linkage with One District One Product (ODOP) and ONDC.
accepted.tq: Combine the territorial norm with the two stated market-linkage components.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: The maximum equity grant available under the 10,000 FPO scheme is correctly stated as
o: ₹2,000 per farmer member, subject to ₹15 lakh per FPO
₹15 lakh per farmer member, subject to ₹2,000 per FPO
₹18 lakh per farmer member, subject to ₹2 crore per FPO
₹2,000 per FPO, subject to ₹15 crore per farmer
accepted.x: The equity grant is up to ₹2,000 per farmer member, with a maximum of ₹15 lakh per FPO.
accepted.tq: Keep the per-member ceiling separate from the aggregate FPO ceiling.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the credit guarantee and management support under the 10,000 FPO scheme?
o: Credit guarantee up to ₹15 lakh per FPO and management support of ₹2,000 per member
Credit guarantee up to ₹18 lakh per FPO and management support of ₹2 crore over five years
Credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore per FPO and management support of ₹18 lakh per FPO over three years
Credit guarantee up to ₹6,865 crore per FPO and management support of ₹75 lakh per mandi
accepted.x: The scheme provides a credit guarantee of up to ₹2 crore per FPO and management support of ₹18 lakh per FPO over three years.
accepted.tq: Match each financial figure with its correct type of support and beneficiary unit.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the reported FPO status as on 1 January 2026?
accepted.x: The reported status was 56.32 lakh farmers, of whom 21.96 lakh were women, by 1 January 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total beneficiary count from the women-beneficiary subset.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: The reported number of FPOs on e-NAM and ONDC respectively was
accepted.x: The reported figures were 5,048 FPOs on e-NAM and 6,070 FPOs on ONDC.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the two digital platforms while comparing their FPO counts.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of FPOs in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25?
o: 455 FPOs registered; 99 seed, 97 fertiliser and 98 pesticide licences; 207 FPOs on ONDC
13 FPOs registered; 455 seed licences; 207 district committees
455 FPOs registered; 98 seed, 97 fertiliser and 99 pesticide licences; 207 FPOs on e-NAM
207 FPOs registered; 455 on ONDC; 99 pesticide licences only
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh reported 455 registered FPOs, 99 seed licences, 97 fertiliser licences, 98 pesticide licences and 207 FPOs on ONDC.
accepted.tq: Compare the licence categories carefully and reject swapped figures or platforms.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s: District-level monitoring committees for FPOs in Andhra Pradesh were reported in
accepted.x: District-level monitoring committees, or D-MCs, were reported in 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the exact administrative count rather than confusing it with market or platform figures.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the principal economic rationale of the 10,000 FPO scheme?
1. Strengthening farmers' bargaining power
2. Achieving economies of scale
3. Lowering costs
4. Transferring land ownership to FPOs
accepted.x: The scheme aims to strengthen bargaining power, achieve economies of scale and lower costs. It does not transfer land ownership to FPOs.
accepted.tq: Separate the scheme's collective-market objectives from an unrelated land-ownership claim.
accepted.sec: FPOs - 10,000 FPO scheme, SFAC and NABARD role
